spec: Ruled 2026-10-03 (Andrew, DECISIONS.md 'eleven tier 0 weapons nobody fields are cut: the nine the authoring pass invented, the Fishing Net and the Slingshot'): 'Yeah, remove all of those 11.' Delete eleven item rows, each with the attacks it grants, from the authored sources. In content/gen/weapons.json: item.hand-axe, item.sharpened-stake, item.carpenters-mallet, item.cart-chain, item.fishing-net, item.pot-lid, item.broken-bottle, item.rusted-crossbow, item.trappers-claws, item.practice-sword. In content/gen/settled-items.json: item.slingshot. Nothing else is cut: the Fishing Net a hero's power grants (heroes.json, 'Grants spell: Fishing Net') is a spell and stays, and item.net (the Waystation trinket) stays. Then run the content pipeline and ship it (content: npm run check, node ship.mjs --dry, node ship.mjs) so that nothing generated still carries a cut row: hbt-content.json, the codex pages and root CODEX.md, FUNCTIONS.md, the gap lists, the engine pack (engine/src/content/generated/pack.ts), engine/generated/movements.*, the kingdom's generated items and progress, the viewer's generated/static.json. Totals that count items or attacks move with the build - read them off it, never type them. csv/HBT-items.csv (root) lists all eleven: find the tool that writes it and run it; no writer was found in tools/, content/, engine/tools or kingdom/tools on 2026-10-03, so if there is none it is a kept sheet and the eleven lines are deleted from it, said so in the commit. Hand-written files that name a cut row (grep '(item|attack)\.<slug>' over content, engine, kingdom, viewer, tools on 2026-10-03): content/gen/bestiary-test.json:154 - a test unit fires attack.rusted-crossbow.bolt; give it attack.crossbow.bolt, the tier 1 Crossbow's. content/settled.json:432 - a source note that names attack.pot-lid.bash in prose; history, left as it is unless the linter reads it. content/test/damage-packets.test.mjs:29-34 - edits attack.hand-axe.chop; move to an attack that stays. content/V2-DAMAGE-PACKETS.md:20 - the Hand Axe's onCrit +4 case; a dated record, so add one dated line that the row was cut and rewrite nothing. engine/test/damage-packets.test.ts:222 and engine/tools/compare-packet-transition.mts:74 - the Hand Axe case beside the Bane Blade's. engine/test/unit-mods.test.ts:23-24 and 144 - item.hand-axe and item.pot-lid as the worn items, item.cart-chain as an item the unit does not carry. kingdom/test/isc-062.test.ts:25 and 36 - item.cart-chain as a chain-tagged stash item that is not counted. Each test keeps what it proves and moves to a row that stays; the commit says which row replaced which (Law 10, so the landing is done-needs-review). Grep again before landing: a golden, a snapshot or a proving plan may name one too. Not this item's, do not touch: the weapon card set under assets/characters/oathblade-armor/rebuild/candidates/weapon-card-references and weapon-card-models (prompts-v2.json, cards-v2.json, run.json) - Codex is writing those files. Prior art: none - a removal, no new mechanism, name or row.
expect: No item.<slug> or attack.<slug>.* for the eleven is left in content/gen, hbt-content.json, CODEX.md, csv/HBT-items.csv, the engine pack, the kingdom's generated items or the viewer's static dump; the content suite passes and expect.mjs stays at its count; the engine, kingdom and viewer suites pass with the moved fixtures; the control battles are byte-identical, since no unit fielded any of the eleven - a moved baseline is a finding, reported, not accepted.

Duplication review 2026-09-28, findings C1 C2 C5 C8 C9 C21 K7. Andrew: 'Crit base 3 should be counted once.' '2, 5, 15 XP by tier.' (1) Crit: the engine's base 3 (pipeline.ts critChanceOf) is the rule; the converter publishes each unit's authored crit minus 3 (hero rogue +2, warrior 0); enemy crit values authored as totals are published the same way — list every enemy row whose crit changes in the landing (C1). spec: NOT A DEFECT — Angela: the Mage/Ranger split is intentional. The Mage deals MAGIC damage and the Ranger PHYSICAL, which diverge sharply once enemies carry armor; and the Mage has Arcane Bolt and more to come, while the Ranger is essentially just its attack. Raw damage-per-swing is therefore the wrong yardstick. What is still worth measuring: the staff is only distinguishable from the bow against a target with armor > 0, and every enemy in the game today has armor 0. Add an armored enemy, then sweep staff vs bow against it.
expect: against an armored enemy the Mage out-damages the Ranger, and against an unarmored one it does not — the split is visible in the sweep, not just in the design
note: Open question that IS real: attack.mage.strike was used 0 times in 300 battles, the same dead-content shape as Massive Strike. The melee option on a ranged unit may never be worth taking. Unblocked 2026-09-28 (Andrew, DECISIONS.md 'the staff-vs-bow check runs against the Codex's armored enemies'): unit.brute was closed as superseded; sweep against the Codex's armored bestiary rows (unit.skeleton armor 1, unit.bruiser-demon armor 4, ...) and an unarmored one.
